title: Polynomial-size constant-gap relaxation for minimum knapsack
formal: Do universal constants C≥1 and k exist such that every feasible binary-encoded minimum-knapsack instance has an objective-independent rational extended LP relaxation of total encoding length at most (L+1)^k times a universal constant, with integrality gap at most C for every nonnegative cost vector?
definitions:
An instance consists of n≥1 nonnegative integral sizes a_i and a positive integral demand b, with \(\sum_i a_i\ge b\). Its feasible set is \(F=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\}\), and L is the full binary encoding length of (a,b). An extended relaxation is a rational polyhedron Q in variables (x,z), using any finite number of auxiliary continuous variables z, whose projection R onto x satisfies \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\subseteq R\subseteq[0,1]^n\). It may depend on (a,b) but must be chosen before the cost vector. Total encoding length counts dimensions, inequalities, equations and all rational coefficient numerators and denominators.

For each real c≥0 define IP(c)=min over F of c-transpose-x and LP(c)=min over R of the same objective. The condition is IP(c)≤C LP(c) for every c≥0. This multiplicative inequality handles zero optima without division: if LP(c)=0, IP(c) must also be zero. The question is existence of formulations with one uniform polynomial bound; it does not require a polynomial-time construction. Total rational bit size is the selected precise interpretation of size.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of such uniform formulations and gap bounds, or refute their existence. A separate relaxation tailored to each cost vector, or a quasipolynomial-size bound, does not meet the target.
context: Objective-independent formulations must simultaneously approximate all covering objectives. An approximation algorithm for one objective does not automatically supply such a polyhedron.
why: This separates efficient approximate optimization from the existence of a uniformly compact relaxation.

import_provenance.original_title: A polynomial-size constant-gap relaxation for minimum knapsack
import_provenance.original_statement: Does every minimum-knapsack covering instance admit an objective-independent extended linear relaxation of polynomial size with a universal constant integrality gap for all nonnegative costs? This continues Bienstock’s study of knapsack inequalities; known quasi-polynomial-size constant-gap formulations do not settle it.

sentences: A minimum-knapsack instance asks which items cover a demand.
One extended relaxation must work for every nonnegative cost vector.
Its total rational description length must be polynomial in the input length.
A universal constant bounds the multiplicative integrality gap even at zero optima.
Quasipolynomial-size constant-gap formulations fall short of this target.
